clue.text: Team upset about court decrees

indicators.note: about means the turned team word goes around the court abbreviation
in a down clue, upset means the word for team is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A sports side, beaten in a shock, take issue with rulings handed down by a court.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts are official orders issued by an authority, which is what decrees are.

clue.text: Frenchman in France with much of beat that's very busy

parts.note: F is the international abbreviation for France
René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: much of means the word for beat loses its final letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: a tick is a beat, as of a clock

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in France keeps up a frantic pace with the beat of a busy life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' drops the K from TICK, leaving TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frantic and wildly hectic, describing someone or something very busy.

clue.text: Star outwardly operating in manufactured kit's a bluffer

indicators.note: in says the star and outer letters go inside the rearranged kit letters
manufactured means the letters of kit's are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: an idol is a star, a celebrity

indicators.note: outwardly says take only the outside letters of the word operating

explanation.surface: A celebrity is seen performing in kit made for the occasion, putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges only the letters of kit's; 'in' then places the star and the outer letters of 'operating' inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidology is the art of deceiving or teasing people, so one who practises it is a bluffer.

clue.text: Republican consumed by selfishness sent up as fearsome sort

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the whole is read from bottom to top
consumed by means the Republican letter is swallowed inside the word for selfishness

parts.note: ego, an inflated sense of self, stands for selfishness

explanation.surface: A Republican politician is eaten up by selfishness and mocked as a frightening figure.
explanation.walkthrough: R inside EGO makes ERGO; 'sent up' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant of folklore, and by extension any frightening, cruel person.

clue.text: A petition's developed in plant

indicators.note: developed means the letters of a petition's have grown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A petition has gathered support and grown into something bigger in a factory or works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like an industrial site; it is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican shrub with bright red leaves, popular as a Christmas houseplant.

clue.text: Opinion about lecturer — it could be clipped?

indicators.note: about means the word for opinion goes around the lecturer abbreviation

parts.note: 'my bet is' expresses an opinion, so bet can mean an opinion

explanation.surface: A view is offered on a lecturer, who might deserve a clip round the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt fastens with a buckle or clip, as a seat belt is clipped in place.

clue.text: Sound reproduction beginning to emerge in renovated store

indicators.note: in says the first letter of emerge goes inside the reworked store letters
renovated means the letters of store are done up in a new order
beginning to says take the first letter of emerge

explanation.surface: Music starts to come out of a shop that has just been refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' turns STORE into STERO, with E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is equipment for playing recorded sound through two channels, a system of sound reproduction.

clue.text: Allow time amid hurry to get cheese

indicators.note: amid means the allow and time letters go in the middle of the word for hurry

parts.note: to race is to hurry
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Someone in a rush is told to take a moment before fetching the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Raclette is a Swiss cheese, melted and scraped onto potatoes, and also the dish made from it.

clue.text: Director ordering supply for adventurous feats

indicators.note: supply here is the adverb of supple, so the letters of ordering are bent flexibly into a new order

explanation.surface: A director arranges provisions for daring exploits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' reads as a noun; it is the adverb 'supplely', bending ORDERING into ERRINGDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic, daring action, the stuff of bold exploits.

clue.text: Additional section of text raised

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An extra part of a document has been brought up for discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra and additional both mean more than the usual amount, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Suggest chapter about celebrity

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
note is fame or distinction, celebrity, as in a person of note

explanation.surface: A chapter is put forward that discusses a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: To connote is to imply something beyond the literal meaning, which is to suggest it.

clue.text: Note one that's certain to be a success

definitions.meaning: in music a note neither sharp nor flat, marked with its own sign

definitions.text: one that's certain to be a success
definitions.meaning: a person with an inborn gift, bound to succeed at something

explanation.definitionFit: A natural is both an unaltered musical note and someone born with talent who is sure to succeed.

clue.text: Sweets at intervals selected for group

indicators.note: at intervals selected says pick the first, third and fifth letters of the word sweets, skipping the others

explanation.surface: Sweets are picked out now and then to make up a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a collection of things belonging together, such as a group of people or objects.

clue.text: You won't hate eccentric no longer in favour

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of you won't hate are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reassures you that an oddball who has fallen from grace won't be disliked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something or someone on the way out is declining and becoming unfashionable or unpopular, falling from favour.

clue.text: Unusual strain on defender of the status quo that's not permanent

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of strain are set in a different order

parts.note: a Tory, a member of Britain's Conservative Party, is by name a conserver of things as they are

explanation.surface: An odd strain on a conservative leaves a mark that will not last.
explanation.definitionFit: Transitory means passing or lasting only a short time, the opposite of permanent.

clue.text: Male performing in a single TV programme without introduction needs warning

indicators.note: in says the male and performing letters go inside the shortened programme word
without introduction means the word for a single TV programme loses its first letter

parts.note: one edition is a single episode of a broadcast series
on means performing, as an actor is on stage

explanation.surface: A man appearing in one broadcast needs to be told off without being introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without introduction' takes E off EDITION, leaving DITION, into which MON goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An admonition is a reprimand or caution, a warning given to someone about their conduct.

clue.text: Greek character trailing in this way Black Sea resort

indicators.note: trailing means the Greek letter comes behind, after the word for in this way

parts.note: so means in this way, as in 'do it so'
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek visitor lags behind on the way to a seaside holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sochi is a Russian resort city on the Black Sea coast, host of the 2014 Winter Olympics.

clue.text: Conventional sketches, say, from the south in visual range

indicators.note: in says the upturned art word goes inside the word for visual range

parts.note: sight is the range within which things can be seen

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: sketches are an example of art

explanation.surface: Ordinary drawings are seen coming up from below within view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sketches, say' gives the general word by example; 'from the south' works because this is a down clue, read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight can mean conventional or conservative, the opposite of unorthodox.

clue.text: Cunning group in particular

indicators.note: group in says a cluster of letters is gathered inside the word particular

explanation.surface: A sly band is singled out for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean craft or guile, a skill used to deceive, which is cunning.

clue.text: Fly fighter round Germany and Spain

indicators.note: round means the fighter word goes around the Germany letter

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A warplane circles Germany and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny two-winged insect, a kind of fly, often found in swarms.

clue.text: Decline shown by scholar in destiny representative of a country?

parts.note: a dip is a decline or drop

indicators.note: in says the scholar letters go inside the word for destiny

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny
MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A learned person's fall seems to be fated, as befits a national envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is an official who represents their country abroad, such as an ambassador.

clue.text: A star hiring ground perfectly in order

indicators.note: ground means crushed, as in a mill, so the letters of a star hiring are milled into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity hires a ground, and everything is in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'right as rain' means perfectly fine or in good order.

clue.text: Such on reflection talks over time endlessly?

definitions.text: Such on reflection talks over time endlessly?

indicators.note: on reflection means the whole is mirrored, read backwards
in a down clue, over means the talks word sits above the shortened time word

parts.note: gabs means talks idly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for time loses its last letter

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone who chatters on for ages is exactly the sort described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: 'Such' points to the kind of person who talks endlessly, and the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is a person who talks too much, chattering on and on without end.

clue.text: Favoured exercise by first of treadmills

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school

indicators.note: first of says take the opening letter of treadmills

explanation.surface: A preferred workout involves the first of the treadmills at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet project or pet subject is a favoured, especially cherished one.

clue.text: Nameless youth, tense with sign of hesitation, gets to wobble

indicators.note: nameless means the abbreviation for name, the letter N, is dropped from the youth word

parts.note: a teen is a young person
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: An anonymous, nervous young person hesitates and starts to wobble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' takes N (name) out of TEEN, leaving TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to sway unsteadily, as if about to fall, which is to wobble.

clue.text: Check source of problems in cricket, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the first letter of problems goes inside the insect word

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect

indicators.note: source of says take the first letter of problems

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire looks into the root of the trouble in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' suggests the game; here it is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, or check, something.

clue.text: Noise that resounds among fine choristers

indicators.note: among says the letters are found sitting inside the words fine choristers

explanation.surface: A ringing sound is heard among a group of good singers.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back off a surface so that it is heard again.

clue.text: Hazard for motorists? This is concealed in Dorset town

indicators.note: in says the shortened word goes inside the name of the Dorset town

parts.note: Poole is a port town in Dorset, a county on England's south coast

indicators.note: concealed says the following word is hidden away, taken out of the word before it

explanation.surface: A road hazard lies hidden somewhere in a south-coast English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is concealed' reads as plain grammar, but it tells you to remove IS from 'This', leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hole in a road surface that can damage vehicles, so a danger to drivers.

clue.text: Speck found on back of percussive instrument

indicators.note: found on means the speck word comes before the letter that follows it

parts.note: a pip is a small spot or speck

indicators.note: back of says take the final letter of percussive

explanation.surface: A tiny mark is spotted on the back of a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'percussive instrument' reads as one phrase; 'percussive' only gives its last letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a simple wind instrument, a tube blown to make a sound.

clue.text: Part of a contest next to hospital in uncultivated land

parts.note: a heat is a preliminary round of a race or competition
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A qualifying round is held beside a hospital on open ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A heath is an area of open, wild land covered with heather and coarse grass.

clue.text: Villain concerned with investigation about a contract's conclusion

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to

indicators.note: about means the investigation word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a probe is an investigation

indicators.note: conclusion says take the last letter of contract's

explanation.surface: A criminal is the subject of an inquiry into how a deal was wrapped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled, morally depraved person, a rogue or villain.
